{{DISPLAYTITLE:Interiors in ''Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas''}}{{Disambiglink|For other uses, see [[Interiors]].}}
[[File:InteriorWorld-GTASA-Int0to3Example.gif|right|250px|An Enter-Exit arrow teleporting the player from a ground level location in Int 0 to a high altitude location in Int 3.]]
'''Interiors''' are a part of the environment in {{SA}}.

==Description==
Building interiors are first made visible with the series' transition to full 3D graphics with the release of {{III}}.

In ''Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas'', most of the interiors are placed in empty parallel worlds, usually high above the aircraft height limits. The player is teleported to these interiors through the yellow [[ENEX|Enter-Exit]] arrows found in front of certain building entrance doors in the "exterior world". The function of these yellow arrows is to teleport the player from the entrance of the building to the corresponding interior of the building.

These separate "worlds" consists of replicas of the in-game map, where the main map's terrain and objects, except for their collision models, are completely unloaded and invisible, while each individual building interior model is made visible.

===Ambience Sounds===
Similarly to the interiors in {{VC}}, certain interiors have unique ambience sounds.
*Fast food restaurants have cutlery and fryer sounds.
*Fancy restaurants have unique ambience music (although muted during their only appearance in the dating activity cutscenes).
*Tuning garages, wardrobes and other interiors have in-game radio stations playing in the background.

===Particle Effects===
Particle effects used in interiors such as fire, water and smoke are loaded in the exterior world, although not normally visible without using glitches and exploits.

===Dynamic Objects===
Dynamic objects that can be moved through the player's interactions or mission script are normally visible in the world. This includes physical doors used to load interiors, garage doors and interactive cranes.

===Skybox and Weather Presets===
The skybox is present inside interiors, and has two variations.
*The '''colored skybox''' is used to simulate the exterior world's skybox and its weather presets. However, it does not feature particle effects such as clouds, rainbows or rain. It is mainly used for interiors with visible "fake" exterior, such as [[Marco's Bistro]] and [[World of Coq]].
*The '''black skybox''' is intended for interiors without any visible exterior (windows closed). Despite the visual darkness, the weather presets and dynamic light sources are normally applied to the world itself. It is mainly used by ''all'' interiors that are normally loaded by ENEX arrows and mission markers, including all clothing stores, barber shops, restaurants, and it simulates the black ceiling inside stadiums.

If the interior is loaded using the wrong skybox through exploits such as teleportation, it will be subject to glitches (usually mirrors not being rendered).

{{Gallery
|InteriorWorld-GTASA-NormalSkybox-WeatherPresets.gif|Several weather presets and time of day showcased on [[Saint Mark's]] (intended colored skybox).
|InteriorWorld-GTASA-DarkSkybox.gif|Several weather presets and times of day showcased on Saint Mark's (black skybox).
|InteriorWorld-GTASA-DarkSkybox-EffectonTextures.gif|Interior light sources in models and textures, tied to in-game time (independent from the skybox).
}}

There are in total 18 different interior worlds, not including the exterior world where the San Andreas map is rendered. The following list includes all of the available interiors and their respective coordinates in the world map, including unused interiors.

===PlayStation 2 Exclusive Content===
====Additional Ammu-Nation Inacessible Room====
{{Beta|game=SA|type = building}}
In the [[PlayStation 2]] version, two of the existing [[Ammu-Nation (3D Universe)|Ammu-Nation]] interiors (the [[Downtown Los Santos (3D Universe)|Downtown Los Santos]] and [[Queens]] branches) have a large, inaccessible empty room located next to the shooting range, behind the door at the side of the room. This, along with [[Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Props#Rifle Range Targets|unused targets]] of characters from ''GTA III'', implies that an extra shooting range challenge, similar to the one featured in [[The Shootist]]/[[Rifle Range]] in ''GTA Vice City'', was planned at some point in development. This room was cut in all subsequent ports.<ref>https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q7z96t8D0xQ</ref>

Normally, the room can only be seen from the outside by using a [[jetpack]] to navigate all the way to the interior. The ceiling can only be seen from certain angles, becoming fully invisible if it is landed on. The ceiling, the walls and the floor are all solid, indicating that the room was not a last minute addition. Looking from the room towards the shooting range, a space may be seen in a wall from certain angles, instead of the door that can be properly seen if looking from the shooting range towards the empty room.

{{Gallery
|Ammu-Nation-GTASAps2-UnusedRoom1.png|The unused room viewed from the ceiling. Note the glitched shadows of the door that connects it to the shooting range.
|Ammu-Nation-GTASAps2-UnusedRoom2.png|Yet another angle from the ceiling. Notice how the door looks different from this angle.

==Oversights==
===Unlocking Mission Interiors===
Due to a glitch involving the Jetpack cheat in the introductory mission [[In the Beginning]], certain interior ENEX arrows available only through mission script can be unlocked.

If the player enables the Jetpack cheat during the [[Police (vehicle)|Police Car]] segment, while Carl is inside the vehicle, the mission won't be able to throw him out of the car in the alleyway in order to progress. Instead, the player is [[Wasted]] and sent to the nearby hospital.

Afterwards, seven ENEX arrows are unlocked in the map. All of these arrows are intended to be available during missions only, and unavailable before and after completing the mission (except for the [[Ammu-Nation (3D Universe)|Ammu-Nation]], which is temporarily disabled until its introduction).

===Smoke Generators===
Due to a glitch in the [[PC]] version{{vague|not tested on consoles}}, smoke particle generators used in interiors ([[Millie Perkins]]'s bedroom torches/[[Cluckin' Bell (3D Universe)|Cluckin' Bell]] fryers) may be visible from afar by the player: if the interior is entered, the particles are generated for a few seconds, after which the player can exit the interior and quickly look at the interior's location in the sky.

The Fort Carson Cluckin' Bell is the easiest area to use to spot the smoke particles in the sky, due to its close proximity to the Cluckin' Bell sky interior location.
